axes.brief:
Competitive elections, presidential recall and constitutional review coexist with ruling-party dominance, judicial pressure and weak accountability.
Focused six-question reassessment: Popular consultation and presidential recall provide qualified direct participation, with subject exclusions and constitutional requirements. Defined presidential succession is not a free governing-party choice; emergency powers retain congressional constraints.
axes.counterEvidence:
2026court relief shows operative review despite independence concerns; judicial-election and foreign-interference proposals are not automatically enacted unilateral presidential powers.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. Popular consultation and presidential recall provide qualified direct participation, with subject exclusions and constitutional requirements. Defined presidential succession is not a free governing-party choice; emergency powers retain congressional constraints.

answers.rationale: Actual competitive presidential/congressional elections remain operative; ruling-party dominance and violence qualify equal electoral implementation.

The retained sourced research records: Competitive elections, presidential recall and constitutional review coexist with ruling-party dominance, judicial pressure and weak accountability. Focused interpretation: Popular consultation and presidential recall provide qualified direct participation, with subject exclusions and constitutional requirements. Defined presidential succession is not a free governing-party choice; emergency powers retain congressional constraints. This is delegation of policy decisions to independent specialists, not replacement of the electorate or a claim that all expertise is political sovereignty. A legislative mandate, appointment process and later review can coexist with not voting on every operational decision.  The described institutional delegation or bounded permission makes agreement more likely than disagreement. Legal safeguards, narrower implementation or an inferred historical application make ordinary agreement more appropriate than an unconditional strong response. The citations supply contextual evidence, not a documented exact response to this new wording. The original source dossier is used as retained research; this pass does not claim a fresh retrieval or complete verification of every historical citation. Precise policy scope, hypothetical institutional translations and response intensity remain uncertain.

axes.brief:
Constitutional expression, privacy and personal autonomy coexist with coercive security practice, surveillance and uneven due process.
Focused bank 3.0.0 reassessment: Surveillance and uneven due process support qualified bulk-records and movement-control discretion. Voter credentials are not a general mandatory carry-and-show identity regime. Constitutional search limits compete with coercive actual policing. Constitutional civic association opposes general prior permission despite intimidation and uneven enforcement.
axes.counterEvidence:
Cannabis authorization is selective rather than all drugs legal; SIM identity is not universal online identity, and judicially authorized detention differs from detention with no independent review.
Focused review: distinguish targeted warrants from bulk records, document possession from compulsory carrying, courts in law from effective prompt recourse, and notification/registration from discretionary association permission. Surveillance and uneven due process support qualified bulk-records and movement-control discretion. Voter credentials are not a general mandatory carry-and-show identity regime. Constitutional search limits compete with coercive actual policing. Constitutional civic association opposes general prior permission despite intimidation and uneven enforcement. Earlier evidence limitations remain; new questions do not establish empirical calibration.
